title: A plinth stone from a photograph
note: The other half of the plinth: a photograph of real marble taken apart into four maps and lit in Cycles. There is no honest way to preview one without rendering it - the studio page this replaces could only ever show WHICH RECTANGLE of the photograph lands on the block, which answers `slabs across` and `offset` and is honest about answering nothing else. add-stone.py runs both steps and writes the entry to design/plinth/stones/, which is the door build-slab.py already reads.
needs: Blender on PATH, and a photograph of marble. Neither the photograph nor the maps are committed - what ships is the plate - so a stone can be LISTED from a fresh checkout and only RE-BAKED from a tree that still has the image.

groups.name: The photograph
groups.note: Maps are per IMAGE and not per stone, and they are keyed by the CONTENT of the file: a second bake of the same photograph at a different scale is fifteen seconds of Cycles rather than fifty megabytes of PNG.

params.label: the photograph
params.note: Required. A relative path is read from the repository root.

params.label: the stone's stem
params.note: The STEM and not the key: add-stone.py appends each style to it, so this becomes my-marble-deep and its siblings.

params.label: what it is
params.note: One line, shown beside its plate. Left empty, add-stone.py writes one from the name.

params.label: map size
params.note: The longest edge the maps are built at. One of the two options that changes what the maps ARE, so moving it rebuilds them rather than reusing them.

params.label: square the maps
params.note: The other one. Squares the source before the maps are cut, for a photograph that is not close to the block's own aspect.

groups.name: What is baked
groups.note: One run writes a stone per style, so a bake-off is one command rather than four.

params.label: styles
params.note: Comma-separated. Left empty, add-stone.py uses its own set, which is the four the gemini stones were compared as.

params.label: grade
params.note: Which basecolor ladder is wired in. `asis` is the photograph as taken; `deep` and `gold` are the two the gemini bake-off compared.

params.label: replace an entry that exists
params.note: Off by default, so a name already taken is a refusal rather than a stone that quietly becomes a different one.

params.label: write the entry and do not render
params.note: The maps and the entry, with no Cycles at all. What it is for is checking the window before spending the render.

groups.name: The material
groups.note: Everything here is what the photograph cannot say on its own: how the surface stands off, how far light goes into it, and what is on top of it.

params.label: slabs across the block
params.note: One of the two strongest controls. Below 1 the figure grows and one swathe runs the length of the block; above it the network goes fine and dense. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: offset along the slab
params.note: The other. Which part of the photograph lands on the front face. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: bump, strength and distance
params.note: Two words, because the generator takes two: how much relief, and over what distance in model units. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: subsurface
params.note: How far light goes into the calcite before it comes back out. It is most of what tells marble from painted stone. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: clear coat, weight and roughness
params.note: The polish on top, as two words. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: roughness map strength
params.note: How much of the derived roughness map is wired in. 0 is one flat polish over the lot, which is the deliberately crippled control gemini-plain is. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.

params.label: lay the fracture network over it
params.note: The hybrid: the photograph brings the branching network no noise field can make, and the procedural fracture lays a crisp hairline over the top of it.

params.label: the room
params.note: Which surround it is lit in. Same parameter as the procedural Bake's, and the same angular-size rule stands behind it. Empty is add-stone.py's own behaviour: the STYLE decides, and every style has an answer. A value here overrides the style on every one of them at once, which is a thing to do deliberately rather than by default.
